'''Conrad "Conny" Rudolf Agaton Palm''' (May 31, 1907 – December 27, 1951)<ref>{{Cite web |title=9 (Svenska män och kvinnor : biografisk uppslagsbok / 6. P-Sheldon) |url=https://runeberg.org/smok/6/0021.html |access-date=2023-06-13 |website=runeberg.org |language=sv}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Tekniker dr Conny Palm framför den av honom konstruerade matematikmaskinen Bark, några månader före hans död 1951. |url=https://digitaltmuseum.se/021018293426/tekniker-dr-conny-palm-framfor-den-av-honom-konstruerade-matematikmaskinen |access-date=2023-06-13 |website=digitaltmuseum.se |language=en}}</ref> was a Swedish [[electrical engineer]] and [[statistician]], known for several contributions to [[teletraffic engineering]] and [[queueing theory]].<ref name="telektronikk">[[Rolf B. Haugen]], [http://www.telenor.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/05/T95_2-3.pdf The life and work of Conny Palm – some personal comments and experiences] from ''Telektronikk'' ([[Telenor]] research journal), 2(3):50–55, 1995</ref>

== Education and career ==
Palm enrolled at the School of Electrical Engineering at the [[Royal Institute of Technology]] in [[Stockholm]] in 1925, being awarded his [[M.Sc.]] (1940) and [[Ph.D.]] (1943) on a dissertation entitled ''Intensitätsschwankungen im Fernsprechverkehr'' (Intensity Fluctuations in Telephone Traffic). Palm's work was also joint with [[L. M. Ericsson]], cooperating with [[Christian Jacobæus]]. He attended [[Harald Cramér]]'s queueing theory group, met [[William Feller]] (1937).<ref name="telektronikk"/>
Later, Palm was in the [[Swedish Board for Computing Machinery]] (''Matematikmaskinnämnden''), where he led the project that developed the first Swedish computer, the [[BARK (computer)|BARK]] (1947–51), informally referred to as CONIAC (Conny [Palm] Integrator And Calculator). He was adjunct professor in [[telecommunications]] at Royal Institute of Technology as well.

Professor [[Håkan Sterky]], who was Palm's thesis advisor, has characterised Palm as a [[Bohemianism|bohemian]] and a brilliant statistician. He had started his research before he graduated, which seemed to be due to a lack of interest for some undergraduate courses rather than the level of difficulty of the courses. To apply pressure on him, it was finally agreed that his monthly salary from [[Ericsson]] would only be paid out if he had passed one of his remaining undergraduate exam that month. Sterky related how Palm would typically show up a few days before pay day wishing to sit for an oral exam.<ref>[http://www.e.kth.se/lnk/historia/75jubel/ Kongl. Elektrosektionen 1910–1985: ''Storamiralerna hos Sekreteraren – Samtal med Håkan Sterky''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090820080846/http://www.e.kth.se/lnk/historia/75jubel/ |date=2009-08-20 }} (interview with Håkan Sterky in 1985 on the occasion of the Electrical Engineering Student Association's 75th anniversary), accessed on July 20, 2009 {{in lang|sv}}</ref>
